answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through memory-bound puzzles. Nodes commit volatile storage, forcing verification threads to wander across a dense juniper matrix of pseudo-random pointers. A verification lantern audits query latencies to confirm that tables reside in physical RAM. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning dedicated memory chips per identity. However, this high memory-bandwidth requirement disadvantages lightweight, resource-constrained agents.
